questions.question: A bar of silicon is doped with boron concentration of [latex]10^{16} \text{cm}^{-3}[/latex]  and assumed to be fully ionized. It is exposed to light such that electron-hole pairs are generated throughout the volume of the bar at the rate of [latex]10^{20} \text{cm}^{-3} s^{-1}[/latex]. questions.explanation: Boron [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Acceptor type doping [latex] \begin{aligned} N_{A} &=10^{16} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \\ g_{0 p} &=1020 \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \\ \tau &=100 \mu \mathrm{s} \\ n_{i} &=10^{10} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \end{aligned}[/latex] Product of steady state electron-hole concentration =? At thermal equilibrium (before shining light) [latex] \begin{array}{ll} \text { Hole concentration, } & p_{o} \simeq N_{A}=10^{16} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \\ \text { Electron concentration, } & n_{0}=\frac{n_{i}^{2}}{p_{0}}=\frac{10^{20}}{10^{16}}=10^{4} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \end{array}[/latex] After, illumination of light, Hole concentration, [latex]p=p_{o}+\delta p[/latex] Electron concentration, [latex]\quad n=n_{o}+\delta n[/latex] Due to shining light, excess carrier concentration, [latex] \begin{aligned} \delta p &=\delta n=g_{o p} \cdot \tau=10^{20} \times 100 \times 10^{-6}=10^{16} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \\ \therefore \qquad p &=10^{16}+10^{16}=2 \times 10^{16} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}\\ n&=10^{4}+10^{16} \simeq 10^{16} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \end{aligned}[/latex] So, product of steady state electron-hole concentration [latex] \begin{aligned} &=n p=10^{16} \times 2 \times 10^{16} \\ &=2 \times 10^{32} \mathrm{~cm}^{-6} \end{aligned}[/latex]
